notes: Defect: promo code discount amount is not displayed correctly for return trip tickets in Mozio email confirmations. The codebase has separate handling for return trips (swapping from/to stations in create-reservations.mappers.ts) and for discount mapping (map-to-sanitized-mozio-dispatch.ts passes discount.amount through, apply-report-discounts.service.ts applies report discounts). The return-trip modification path (map-line-item-return-trip-modification.ts) likely fails to propagate or correctly compute the promo/discount amount for the return leg, causing the Mozio email confirmation to show an incorrect or missing promo code amount for return trips.

acceptanceCriteria: Given a one-way trip reservation with an applied promo code discount, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then the promo code discount amount displayed matches the discount that was applied to the reservation.

Given a return trip reservation with an applied promo code discount, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then the promo code discount amount displayed for the return leg matches the discount that was applied to that leg.

Given a return trip reservation with a promo code discount that applies to both the outbound and return legs, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then the discount amount is correctly displayed for each leg and the total discount across both legs equals the expected total promo discount.

Given a return trip reservation where the promo code discount applies only to the outbound leg, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then the outbound leg shows the correct discount amount and the return leg shows zero or no promo discount amount.
Given a return trip reservation with no promo code applied, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then no promo code discount amount is displayed for either the outbound or return leg.

Given a return trip reservation where the promo code discount amount is zero, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then the discount amount displays as zero rather than being omitted or showing an incorrect value.

Given a return trip reservation with a promo code discount, When the reservation data passes through the return-trip modification mapping pipeline, Then the discount amount is preserved and propagated to the final Mozio dispatch output without being lost, overwritten, or reset to an incorrect value.

Given a return trip reservation with a promo code discount, When the from/to stations are swapped for the return leg during reservation creation, Then the discount amount remains correctly associated with the return leg and is not dropped or miscalculated as a side effect of the station swap.

Given a return trip reservation with a promo code discount where the discount amount field is null or undefined in the source data, When the Mozio email confirmation is generated, Then the system handles the missing value gracefully without throwing an error and displays no discount amount rather than an incorrect or corrupted value.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria and a root-cause hypothesis. I built the full AC set from scratch based on the defect description and the technical notes about the files involved. Key additions: (1) AC1 establishes a regression baseline for one-way trips to ensure the fix doesn't break existing behavior. (2) AC2 is the core fix verification for return trips. (3) AC3-AC4 cover edge cases for how discounts distribute across legs. (5) AC5 covers the no-promo baseline. (6) AC6 covers the zero-discount edge case. (7) AC7 verifies discount propagation through the mapping pipeline end-to-end. (8) AC8 specifically targets the suspected root cause — the station swap during return-trip mapping potentially dropping the discount. (9) AC9 covers null/undefined discount amount error handling. All ACs are written as observable outcomes (Given/When/Then) with no implementation instructions.
